speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to understand more about your son's condition. Has he ever been able to pass a stool per rectum, or does he only pass stool through a different opening?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your son ever passed a normal stool through his anus, or has he had a surgical opening (stoma) for bowel movements? I need to clarify his bowel history to rule out conditions like Hirschsprung disease.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby ever passed a meconium stool within the first 48 hours of life, and has he passed any regular stools since then? I need to determine if there is a history of delayed passage of meconium or chronic constipation.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the baby pass meconium within the first 48 hours of life, or was there a significant delay? Also, has a rectal exam been performed to check for an anal stenosis or imperforate anus?

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

The X-ray findings of dilated bowel segments with an empty rectum are classic for Hirschsprung disease. To confirm this diagnosis, I need to assess for the presence of aganglionosis in the distal colon.

REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal rectal biopsy rules out Hirschsprung disease, so we must look for other causes of functional obstruction. Does the baby have a history of chronic diarrhea with foul-smelling stools, and has he been diagnosed with Cystic Fibrosis?
